findings.claim: Listing users has unbounded O(U x O) work and an N+1 repository access pattern, so production-sized data can cause excessive datastore calls or CPU/latency and make the endpoint unavailable under load.
evidence: src/users.py:15-16 iterates over every user returned by list_users() and invokes orders_for_user() separately for each user; there is no pagination or bulk count operation.
src/users.py:9-10 implements each orders_for_user() call as a full scan of all orders, making the in-memory implementation O(number_of_users x number_of_orders).

A runtime probe with 1,000 users observed exactly 1,000 calls to orders_for_user(), confirming that repository work grows linearly with the number of users before accounting for each call's full order scan.
The provided happy-path test passes but covers only two users and two orders, so it does not exercise production-scale behavior.

uncertainties: The case uses an in-memory repository, so the exact production latency and whether each repository call would be a network/database round trip cannot be measured from the provided code; the per-user call pattern and quadratic scan behavior are directly verified.
